item.text: {"piece_id":"02","title":"CAD Agents Can Draft More Than They Can Yet Prove","question":"Which claims withstand scrutiny, and where are the evidence or interpretations in tension?","argument":"The evidence supports frontier models as drafting aids for editable CAD artifacts under defined software harnesses, not as proof that their outputs meet tolerance, manufacturability, or production-approval requirements. Autodesk’s announcements signal a move toward agentic, connected CAD workflows, while NVIDIA’s prescribed workflow shows that converted robotics assets require staged checks. The tension is between claims made at different levels of checking, rather than between opposing results.","synthesis":"MIT-CDFG separates native-CAD benchmark results from untested physical requirements; Cadalyst distinguishes Autodesk features available now from previews, beta, and planned releases; and NVIDIA describes distinct visual, physics, and simulation checks for converted robot CAD. Together, these sources indicate that the relevant unit of evaluation is the workflow and its checks—not a model output or a vendor demonstration alone. A benchmark score, announced connected workflow, or selected simulation grasp test establishes something narrower than manufacturability or dependable physical deployment.","limitations":"This provisional brief uses three independent publishers, but the accepted set contains no podcast evidence, so the series-wide podcast requirement remains unmet. It also contains no clearly evidenced AI-native startup to test; Autodesk and NVIDIA are established vendors, so the startup-watch requirement cannot be met without additional evidence. NVIDIA’s video is represented by an automatic transcript and describes a prescribed validation process rather than pass rates or physical-transfer results.","claims":[{"claim_id":"02-c1","statement":"The MIT-CDFG survey reports that, on 100 native FreeCAD benchmark tasks, leading models average 85% and fully solve about 45 tasks, while tolerance specifications and manufacturability have not been tested on physical parts.","type":"source_claim","evidence":[{"item_id":"feed:https://mit-cdfg.github.io/Survey-AI-for-3D-modeling-Robotics/#view-stats","version_id":"08b1c2cdebb5796d7332d57e8928784a621aec9f82db91448016eaa53ea51fe5","locator":{"type":"text","quote":"On 100 FreeCAD benchmark tasks, the leading models average 85%, up from 70% for GPT-5.6 Sol, and fully solve about 45\n(Parametric CAD Bench 2026)\n. Tolerance specifications and manufacturability have not been tested on physical parts."}}]},{"claim_id":"02-c2","statement":"Cadalyst reports that Autodesk’s Fusion automation and connected-client capabilities have mixed availability, with several larger capabilities still announced or in development.","type":"reported_fact","evidence":[{"item_id":"feed:https://blog.cadalyst.com/cadmanagement/autodesk-university-2026-what-the-announcements-mean-for-cad-teams","version_id":"e991bf7bc957baf20c6e947cff7b9a0d159ef7a1b8b9d5f500f7e1c95d47573b","locator":{"type":"text","quote":"Mixed. Autodesk Assistant capabilities are already appearing in manufacturing products, while several of the larger automation and connected-client capabilities remain announced or in development."}}]},{"claim_id":"02-c3","statement":"NVIDIA’s video describes checking a converted robot asset’s visual properties, scale, parts, and appearance against references before later physics and simulation checks.","type":"source_claim","evidence":[{"item_id":"youtube:H5UaOdIZERw","version_id":"c86fae4c3874c6aa997843fe5a3365bf0a32d21acb0927fbcea32b10e0709a06","locator":{"type":"segment","segment_id":"s0004"}},{"item_id":"youtube:H5UaOdIZERw","version_id":"c86fae4c3874c6aa997843fe5a3365bf0a32d21acb0927fbcea32b10e0709a06","locator":{"type":"segment","segment_id":"s0005"}},{"item_id":"youtube:H5UaOdIZERw","version_id":"c86fae4c3874c6aa997843fe5a3365bf0a32d21acb0927fbcea32b10e0709a06","locator":{"type":"segment","segment_id":"s0006"}}]},{"claim_id":"02-c4","statement":"A CAD-agent capability claim should be limited to the artifact or behavior actually checked, because the accepted evidence does not show that CAD benchmark scores, announced workflows, or selected simulation grasp tests establish manufacturability or physical transfer.","type":"inference","evidence":[{"item_id":"feed:https://mit-cdfg.github.io/Survey-AI-for-3D-modeling-Robotics/#view-stats","version_id":"08b1c2cdebb5796d7332d57e8928784a621aec9f82db91448016eaa53ea51fe5","locator":{"type":"text","quote":"Tolerance specifications and manufacturability have not been tested on physical parts."}},{"item_id":"feed:https://blog.cadalyst.com/cadmanagement/autodesk-university-2026-what-the-announcements-mean-for-cad-teams","version_id":"e991bf7bc957baf20c6e947cff7b9a0d159ef7a1b8b9d5f500f7e1c95d47573b","locator":{"type":"text","quote":"Some of what Autodesk demonstrated is ready to use today.
